Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Malaysia's reply. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. It will be a new opening pair for Malaysia with Nuni and Husna striding out to the centre. Selena Ross has the new ball in hand. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Batting has been Malaysia's Achilles' heel in the tournament, with scores of 23 and 31 in their previous outings. They face a daunting task here as they look to put up a more competitive performance with the bat. Can they rise to the occasion and provide a stern challenge to the West Indies? Back in a bit to find out.

Nazwah is down for a quick chat. She says her favourite player is Alana King because of her consistency and the knack of picking wickets. Adds that they are excited to win this game and have done really well so far.

The arrival of Jahzara Claxton brought some much-needed momentum to the innings, but every time West Indies seemed to be gaining traction, Malaysia managed to strike back. However, their inability to maintain the discipline they displayed in the first 10 overs proved costly. Conceding as many as 27 extras, including 23 wides, Malaysia gave away crucial runs. It could have been a completely different story had they kept their discipline intact throughout the innings.

A good job from Malaysia towards the end to hold West Indies back, conceding just 9 runs from the last 2 overs. It turned out to be a tale of two halves for the Malaysian bowlers. They were disciplined in the first 10 overs, giving away just 37 runs, but the next 10 overs saw their hard work unravel with a mixed bag of bowling, conceding 75 runs. After opting to bowl first, Malaysia displayed excellent discipline with the ball and did not allow West Indies to get away. Their ground fielding was equally impressive, adding pressure to the batters, who managed only 2 boundaries in the first 10 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: With all the pre-match formalities done, it's time for the action to take over! The two umpires make their way out to the middle. Malaysia Women Under-19 are in a big huddle along with the coaching staff. They now take the field and spread across to take their positions. Samara Ramnath and Asabi Callender are the openers for West Indies Women Under-19. Marsya has the new ball and will start the proceedings. Here we go.
Out come the match officials and players from both teams for the national anthems. It will be the anthem of West Indies first followed by that of Malaysia.

PITCH REPORT - Ed Rainsford is in the middle for the pitch analysis. He says the temperature and humidity are high for the day while there are chances of rain later. Adds that it is a 60-yard boundary across the ground and the pitch used for this game is more like a subcontinental one with a little bit of tackiness which could see some assistance for the bowlers and batters will have to counter it by playing straight.

The captain of West Indies Women Under-19, Samara Ramnath says that they were looking to bowl first. Tells that it is all about execution and they will look to do well with the bat. Shares that they have had two tough losses but there have been positives for them to lean on. Informs that they have made three changes.

Nur Dania Syuhada, the skipper of Malaysia Women Under-19 says they will try to give their best in this match and the preparation for this game has been good. Mentions that they have one change in the team.

West Indies Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Asabi Callender, Samara Ramnath (C), Naijanni Cumberbatch, Jahzara Claxton, Amrita Ramtahal, Abigail Bryce, Kenika Cassar, Denella Creese (WK) (In for Kristen Sutherland), Erin Deane (In for Brianna Harricharan), Trisha Hardat (In for Amiah Gilbert), Selena Ross.
Malaysia Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Nuni, Nur Aliya (WK), Husna, Nur Dania Syuhada (C), Suabika, Nur Izzatul Syafiqa, Nuriman, Ain, Adani (In for Nur Isma Dania), Nazwah, Marsya.
TOSS - Malaysia Women Under-19 have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

The West Indies, meanwhile, have struggled to find their rhythm in the tournament so far but will fancy their chances against the tournament debutants. However, discipline with the ball will be crucial, as they conceded a whopping 36 extras in their last game, something they will need to address if they want to secure progression. It’s all to play for, with a spot in the Super Six stage up for grabs! Stay tuned for toss and team news.

Malaysia have had a challenging experience in their maiden Women's Under-19 World Cup. While their previous outing against India showed glimpses of intent with the bat, translating that into tangible success remains a hurdle. To challenge the West Indies, Malaysia will need a collective effort across all three departments.

Hello and a warm welcome to the decisive final day of group stage action! The first game of the day features tournament hosts Malaysia taking on the West Indies in what is effectively a knockout clash in Group A, with the winner securing a spot in the Super Six stage.
... MATCH DAY ...

As the ICC Women’s Under-19 T20 World Cup 2025 progresses, Malaysia Women Under-19 and West Indies Women Under-19 face off in a crucial encounter that will determine the third spot in Group A. Both teams are coming off defeats in their first two matches, making this an important clash for their aspirations to advance to the Super Six stage. Malaysia Women Under-19 struggled significantly in their opening matches, suffering a heavy loss to Sri Lanka, where they were bowled out for a mere 23 runs, followed by another disappointing performance against India, managing only 31 runs. Skipper Nur Dania Syuhada is eager to lead her team to their first victory and will look for improved batting performance to capitalize on the opportunity against the West Indies. On the other hand, West Indies Women Under-19 also encountered challenges with their batting lineup. They recorded a dismal total of 44 runs against India in their opening game, followed by a slightly better but losing performance against Sri Lanka, where they scored 85 runs while chasing a target of 166. The West Indies will be striving to enhance their batting form and turn the tide in their favor in this pivotal showdown. Both teams are keenly aware that only a win will keep their hopes alive in the tournament. The stakes are high as Malaysia looks to leverage home advantage against a struggling West Indies side. Fans can expect a fiercely contested match as both teams aim to secure crucial points and a chance for progression in the tournament.
